info.bio:
La historia se remonta a las antípodas australianas, en la muy escocesa Glasgow, cuando el matrimonio conformado por el Sr. y la Sra. Young, quienes ya para ese enero de 1953 contaban con cinco vástagos en su hogar, vio nacer a su nuevo hijo: Malcolm, el sexto de la cría.

Nadie jamás se hubiera imaginado que el nuevo regalo del Cielo sería más tarde el encargado en tomar iniciativa con respecto a formar una de las más históricas bandas de rock.

own_scenes.desc: «Let There Be Rock» es para Weinstein el texto paradigmático sobre la genealogía del rock vista desde el heavy: el blues (sin pretensiones) recibe una inyección de sentimentalismo pop y nace un híbrido con sus propias cualidades, que llega como un concierto: primero el sonido, luego las luces, luego la batería y la guitarra. Su rayo en el logotipo (idea sacada, dice la tradición, de la máquina de coser de la hermana de Angus Young) y discos como High Voltage y Powerage explotan la imagen de la energía eléctrica. Es el gran cantor del sexo festivo y sin compromiso («Whole Lotta Rosie», «Shoot to Thrill») y del infierno como fiesta («Highway to Hell», «Hell Ain’t a Bad Place to Be»).

notes.chapter: Cap. 3: Hacer la música: los dioses del metal
notes.text: Cuando murió Bon Scott, su cantante talentoso y alcohólico, lo lloraron pero lo sustituyeron con éxito por Brian Johnson. La prensa metal recalca su origen obrero, como el de los «duros» de Birmingham de Black Sabbath.

notes.chapter: Cap. 6: El concierto: la epifanía metal
notes.text: Angus Young hace «sprints de seis cuerdas» de un lado a otro del escenario (se calcula que casi 5.000 kilómetros en una década) y se mete entre el público a hombros de Bon Scott o de un roadie sin dejar de tocar.

refs.q: Perhaps the paradigmatic text in regard to rock and roll’s genealogy is AC/DC’s song “Let There Be Rock.”
refs.para: Heavy metal has produced texts that offer their own history of rock and roll. Perhaps the paradigmatic text in regard to rock and roll’s genealogy is AC/DC’s song “Let There Be Rock.”³ For AC/ DC, rock and roll was a genuine eruption, not a product of an insensible and continuous evolution of musical forms. Rock and roll was something uniquely new when it arose in 1955.
refs.chapter: Cap. 2: Heavy metal: la bestia que se niega a morir

refs.q: AC/DC has exploited the imagery to the fullest extent, placing a lightning bolt in the middle of its name, which itself refers to electrical currents.
refs.para: Typefaces are often embellished with a thunderbolt motif. Bands such as AC/DC and UFO, among others, incorporate the symbol of lightning, standing for released energy, into their logos. AC/DC has exploited the imagery to the fullest extent, placing a lightning bolt in the middle of its name, which itself refers to electrical currents. Tradition has it that AC/DC got the idea from the back of band member Angus Young’s sister’s sewing machine. The group has done albums entitled High Voltage and Powerage. The cover of the latter shows a very jolted Angus, electrical wires emerging from his jacket sleeves, illuminated by an aura of shocking light, which is also seen in his eyes and mouth. The typeface also looks as if it had been shattered by lightning.
refs.chapter: Cap. 2: Heavy metal: la bestia que se niega a morir

refs.q: When Bon Scott, the talented and alcoholic singer for AC/DC, died, he was mourned but nonetheless successfully replaced by Brian Johnson.
refs.para: The strains of interdependence among members of a group are probably responsible for the rancorous accusations that are often made when someone leaves a band. Interdependence also partly explains the legendary solidarity of some groups. For example, Def Leppard’s drummer lost his hand in an automobile accident, but he was not replaced. The band waited for him to heal and then returned to record and tour rather triumphantly with a one-handed drummer. In a less dramatic case, the Scorpions’s distinctive vocalist, Klaus Meine, suffered severe throat problems. He required surgery and could not work for a long time, and it was not clear that he would recover sufficiently to take up his role with the band again. The rest of the band waited patiently and Meine recovered fully. Led Zeppelin broke up when drummer John Bonham died rather than try to replace him, but that is an exceptional case for a successful band. When Bon Scott, the talented and alcoholic singer for AC/DC, died, he was mourned but nonetheless successfully replaced by Brian Johnson. Metallica went on to greater fame with a replacement for bassist Cliff Burton, who died when the band’s touring van overturned. Ozzy sincerely mourned the gruesome death of guitar-ace Randy Rhoads, but went on to find a replacement.
refs.chapter: Cap. 3: Hacer la música: los dioses del metal

refs.q: Angus Young, AC/DC’s guitarist, constantly does “six-string wind sprints” from one side of the stage to the other
refs.para: The value of the blue-collar worker is shown by representing the exertion of work. Displays of energy are universally demanded of the singer and drummer. They serve to embody, literally and figuratively, the value of work. Angus Young, AC/DC’s guitarist, constantly does “six-string wind sprints” from one side of the stage to the other; it has been estimated that in one decade he had traveled almost 3, 000 miles on stage.⁴⁰ Sets have ramps, or at least a drum riser, permitting the singer to move up and down. The folkie astride a stool and the crooner planted all evening at the mike stand are excluded by the code of heavy metal. One key to a metal performance is the power of its passionate activity.

scenes.name: El PMRC y las audiencias del Senado
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: El Parents Music Resource Center, fundado por esposas de políticos de Washington, lleva en 1985 la «música obscena» al Senado de Estados Unidos en las audiencias sobre el etiquetado de discos. Allí el musicólogo Joe Stuessy, asesor del PMRC, declara que el heavy actual es categóricamente distinto de toda música popular anterior porque contiene odio, y el senador Albert Gore pregunta por la tendencia a la violencia explícita, el sexo y el sadomasoquismo «en el área del heavy metal». Para Weinstein es el ejemplo de cómo el género se convierte en asunto público sin que nadie sepa de qué está hablando.

scenes.name: El oficio: del air guitar al dios del metal
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: El músico de heavy sale del público: es el fan que toca la guitarra de aire en el concierto de UFO de 1979 y quiere estar donde está Michael Schenker. No hay escuela ni beca: hace falta talento musical y dramático (actuar la emoción por trescientas veces), un cuerpo joven y atlético (correr y pesas en la gira, el pelo largo como signo de autenticidad) y aprender a vivir en un grupo que no es ni familia ni oficina, con sus «problemas de ego» por la rivalidad entre cantante y guitarrista. El heavy es el estilo más caro de montar y casi no hay clubes donde empezar; el código exige temas propios y autenticidad. Firmar con un sello convierte a la banda en una empresa del capitalismo tardío frente a un oligopolio. El ciclo es componer, grabar (paciencia; el primer disco de Black Sabbath se hizo en doce horas, Spreading the Disease de Anthrax en cinco meses) y girar (aguante: esperar, esperar). La recompensa no es el dinero sino el carisma del chamán que alcanza el éxtasis dionisíaco ante miles de personas; el precio, «quemarse o apagarse», porque nadie que viva lo bastante puede cumplir el código.

scenes.name: Heavy metal de los setenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: «Born To Be Wild» de Steppenwolf acuña la expresión «heavy metal», que pasa a designar en EE UU el hard rock. Blue Oyster Cult definen el nuevo género (satanismo y serie B envueltos en riffs crudos); Aerosmith lo enlazan con el rhythm'n'blues depravado de Stones y Stooges; Kiss abrazan todos los estereotipos; AC/DC, las tripas del rock'n'roll (Back In Black); Journey y Boston, arquetipos del pop-metal; Rush reinventan el power-trio.

podcast.title: 1980 High Voltage Tour at Kiel Opera House
podcast.body: AC/DC's "High Voltage Tour" took place on September 18, 1980, at the Kiel Opera House. The concert was heavily promoted, with tickets available at various outlets including Backstage Records, Lane Co-op, Spectrum, Peaches, the Kiel Opera House box office, and through Dial Tix. "Plug into the 1980 AC DC high voltage tour. E-lectrophying. Scorching AC DC live in concerts of September 18 at the Kiel opera house."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Weird History of Concert Tickets Part 2

podcast.title: Four Lead Singers – Bon Scott Died 1980, Brian Johnson Made Back in Black, Axl Rose Subbed in 2016
podcast.body: AC/DC has had four lead singers. Dave Evans was the original, present from the band's 1973 formation through their glam-rock phase. Bon Scott replaced him after being discovered working as the band's chauffeur; he recorded seven albums cementing AC/DC's reputation but died of acute alcohol poisoning on February 19, 1980. Brian Johnson replaced him in time for *Back in Black* (1980), which has sold at least 50 million copies. When Johnson developed serious ear problems in 2016, Axl Rose of Guns N' Roses sang for approximately two dozen shows; Johnson subsequently received treatment and rejoined. "The swap worked way better than anyone could have dreamed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Softened Stance on Sampling (2007)
podcast.body: By 2007, when the Beastie Boys had become hugely successful, AC/DC softened their stance on sampling. They gave their blessing for the reissue of "Rock Hard" in Europe, with their peers saying, "Aw, mates, do what you want. We don't care anymore." "However, that single was reissued in Europe with AC-DC's Blessing in 2007."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Arrest for Threats and Drug Possession (2014)
podcast.body: In 2014, Phil Rudd was arrested at his home in New Zealand on charges of threatening to kill one person and attempting to hire someone to kill two others. However, the hitman charge fell apart when authorities realized the accuser did not believe the allegations. During a police raid on his home, Rudd was found in possession of cannabis and methamphetamine, for which he was charged. "In 2014, he was arrested at his home in New Zealand on charges of looking to have someone killed."

podcast.body: Billy Corgan of The Smashing Pumpkins openly admired "some of those old ACDC records" for their "pretty great riffs," signifying how 90s alternative artists were embracing and acknowledging the quality of classic hard rock. "Some of those old ACDC records? Pretty great riffs, man."

podcast.body: This classic rock band was played on active rock radio stations in the 2010s as an homage to traditional rock values, alongside new material. "They also played the homage to guns and rouses, NACDC and Led Zeppelin and Van Halen and Ozzy and Sabbath and Death Lepred and Jimmy Hendrix."

podcast.title: Angus Young's Headbanging Style
podcast.body: In the late 1970s, guitarist Angus Young was known for headbanging during AC/DC shows. His energetic stage presence included this vigorous movement. "If you went to an ACDC show in the late 1970s, you would have seen guitarist Angus Young banging his head."

podcast.body: In the early 1980s, Angus Young once made a cup of tea for the speaker during an interview, an example of how "the bigger the artist, the better that they tend to be." "Early, early, early on, this is early 80s, Angus Young of ACDC made me a cup of tea."

podcast.title: Association with Richard Ramirez (The Night Stalker)
podcast.body: AC/DC was the favorite band of serial killer Richard Ramirez, who went on a killing spree in Los Angeles and San Francisco between 1984 and 1986. Ramirez even left a baseball bat with "ACDC" written on it at one murder scene. This association caused the band to be "dogged for years" and labeled as Satanists by those wary of hard rock and metal. "Although Romeroz was a fan, ACDC didn't actually inspire Romeroz to kill, but the band was dogged for years with the association and for a time was branded as Satanists by people who distrusted hard rock and metal."

podcast.body: Bruce Fairbairn produced mega-platinum albums for AC/DC throughout the 1980s and 1990s. "Throughout the 80s and 90s, he produced mega platinum albums for Erasmith and ACDC and Bon Jovi and Inaccess and Kiss and Leverboy and Poison, The Scorpions and Van Halen and a ton of others."

podcast.title: Covered by Dropkick Murphys
podcast.body: AC/DC's songs are being recorded by contemporary hardcore new rock/alt rock/alternative bands like the Dropkick Murphys. This demonstrates a modern trend where genre snobbishness is decreasing, allowing for a broader appreciation of musical aesthetics across different rock subgenres. "And today it's to the point where even hardcore new rock bands, alt rock bands, alternative bands like the Dropkick Murphy's are having fun recording AC DC songs."

podcast.title: Extensive Car Collection
podcast.body: Brian Johnson is an avid car enthusiast with a collection of approximately two dozen vehicles. His collection includes a Morgan, a 1965 Lola T70 Mark I (one of only 15 ever built), a Ferrari, a Jaguar, a Rolls-Royce, a 1928 Bentley, a big block Mustang, several Range Rovers, and a unique 1973 Citroën. He enjoys driving his cars, describing his Morgan as "a lot of fun." "He has about two dozen cars in his collection, including a 1965 Lola T50 Mark I, only 15 of them were ever built."

podcast.title: Former Absence on Spotify
podcast.body: AC/DC's discography was not available on Spotify until recently. While AC/DC has never liked Spotify, the primary reason for the absence was the refusal of the rights owners (not the band itself) to license the music due to royalty disagreements. "no teníamos casi nada la descorracía de ACDC. Esto hoy en día ya está. No lo teníamos, no por la banda, bueno, ACDC si que nunca la ha gustado Spotify, pero no por la banda, sino porque los dueños de los derechos, que no son los artistas se negaban por un tema de diferencias con los Rays Yalpsis."

"We've already talked about how some of the heavy bands of the past saw renewed success, Soundgarden, Metallica, Myron Maiden, ACDC, and so on."

podcast.title: Reunion for Touring
podcast.body: AC/DC was one of many bands from the 60s, 70s, 80s, and 90s that reunited in the 21st century. This trend was primarily driven by financial motivations, as declining CD sales from 2000-2001 led to shrinking royalty revenues for artists, while promoters sought reliable acts to fill large venues and appeal to nostalgic fan demographics with disposable income. "The list of reunions is long."

podcast.title: Strict Anti-Sampling Stance (1980s)
podcast.body: In the 1980s, AC/DC was "categorically against any kind of sampling," which led to the withdrawal of the Beastie Boys' single "Rock Hard" due to illegal samples from "Back in Black." "And even if they had, they wouldn't have got it because AC-DC was categorically against any kind of sampling."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Therapeutic Effects of Music
podcast.body: Dr. Mark Tramos compared AC/DC's music to a "chemo drug" in a music therapy study conducted at Harvard. The band's riffs, beats, melodies, and simple lyrics are noted for hitting all the targets required for therapeutic effect. Listening to AC/DC can improve heart rate and blood pressure, regulate and boost muscle activity, and enhance athletic performance, strength, endurance, and power. Furthermore, surgeons who listen to AC/DC while operating are reported to make fewer mistakes due to the music encouraging focus. For cancer patients, prescribed AC/DC music can significantly reduce anxiety and pain, thereby improving the effectiveness of other medications. "Dr. Mark Tramos says that ACDC can act like a chemo drug. The riffs, the beats, the melodies, and simple lyrics seem to hit all the targets."

xref.title: Mighty Mighty Bosstones – Formed 1983 Boston; Invented Skacore by Mixing Two-Tone with Hardcore; Major Label by 1993
xref.body: The Mighty Mighty Bosstones came together in 1983 when a group of guys became obsessed with the Two-Tone sound despite some members playing in hardcore bands influenced by Motorhead and AC/DC. This combination of Two-Tone ska with American hardcore became known as skacore — annoying to ska purists and initially baffling to hardcore kids, but eventually it clicked. By 1993 they had a major label record deal and a signature look involving plaid suits. "The Boss Tones took two-tone style Skah and made it with American hardcore to create something that was eventually called Skahcore."
